chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayub, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Insulting the believer is mischief (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr), and consuming his flesh is disobedience, and the sanctity of his wealth is like the sanctity of his blood'.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific spiritual consequences of insulting, fighting, or backbiting a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi establishes the sanctity of the believer (al-mu'min) by categorizing specific transgressions against them into distinct spiritual degrees, ranging from major sin to disbelief. It is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence to derive the legal rulings regarding the inviolability of a believer's honor, wealth, and life, emphasizing that these rights are divinely protected. The narration underscores the high status of the believer in Islamic theology, linking social conduct directly to one's spiritual standing.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Insulting the Momin is a mischief and killing him is disbelief, and consuming his flesh (backbiting) is a disobedience, and the sanctity of his wealth is like the sanctity of his blood’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from abu Basir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘

Reviling a believer is a gross sin, fighting him is disbelief, eating his flesh (backbiting) is disobedience and the illegality of consuming his property is like the illegality of spilling his blood (taking his life).”’
